stops.name: Ur Kasdim (Tell el-Muqayyar), the birth of Abram
stops.campa: In the year 1948 of the world a son is born to Terah in the great city under the ziggurat of the moon-god, and they name him Abram. Nimrod's astrologers have read a star that swallows four stars of heaven, and the king would kill every newborn; Terah hides the child. The idols of Ur crowd every threshold. But the boy, alone in a cave, watches the sun cross the sky and the moon rise and set, and reasons his way past every made thing to the One who made them, the Lord who does not rise and does not set.
stops.quote: Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee.

stops.name: Terah's idol-shop, the smashing of the idols
stops.campa: Terah the idol-maker leaves young Abram to mind the shop. A woman comes with a plate of fine flour to set before the gods. Abram takes a staff and smashes them all to shards but the largest, and sets the staff in that one's stone hand. Terah returns raging. Who did this? Abram answers: a woman brought them food, and they quarrelled over who should eat first, and the biggest took the staff and broke the rest. They cannot move, cries Terah, they have no breath! Then why, says the boy, do you serve them?
stops.quote: Have they mouths, that they cannot speak? Do you not see them, that they cannot do good nor evil?

stops.name: The furnace of Nimrod (Balıklıgöl, Şanlıurfa), cast into the fire
stops.campa: Nimrod, whose idols Abram has shamed, builds a fire so vast that no man can come within a bowshot of it. Bound, the young man is flung from the catapult into the heart of the flame. He goes down into fire and walks in its midst untouched; the cords burn from his wrists and nothing else. In the aggadah and the Quran alike God commands the fire, and it obeys. Where the flames stood, a pool of clear water opens; the burning logs turn to carp swimming in it. Abraham walks out unburned, and Nimrod's power is broken.
stops.quote: We said, O fire! Be coolness and safety upon Abraham.

stops.name: Haran (Harran), the sojourn and Terah's death
stops.campa: Terah gathers Abram, Sarai, and Lot and sets out from Ur toward the land of Canaan, but they come to Haran and settle there, in the crossroads-town of caravans and the temple of the moon. Here Terah grows old and dies at two hundred and five years. Abram waits under the vast Mesopotamian sky, herds fattening, the word of the Lord not yet spoken to move him further. The road west lies open beyond the Balikh river.
stops.quote: And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran his son's son, and Sarai his daughter in law... and they came unto Haran, and dwelt there.

stops.name: The Call at Haran: Lech Lecha, the departure at seventy-five
stops.campa: The Lord speaks: Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee. And I will make of thee a great nation. Abram is seventy-five years old. He does not ask where. He takes Sarai his wife and Lot his brother's son and all their substance and the souls they have gotten in Haran, and departs to go into the land of Canaan. The first man to be called out, he goes.
stops.quote: So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.

stops.name: Shechem, the oak of Moreh and the first altar
stops.campa: Abram passes through the land as far as the place of Shechem, to the terebinth of Moreh. The Canaanite is then in the land. Here the Lord appears to him for the first time in Canaan and says: Unto thy seed will I give this land. And Abram builds an altar there to the Lord who has appeared to him, the first stone he raises in the country of the promise, at the pass between Ebal and Gerizim where later Israel will speak its blessings and curses.
stops.quote: And the LORD appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the LORD, who appeared unto him.

stops.name: Bethel, the altar between Bethel and Ai
stops.campa: He removes to the mountain east of Bethel and pitches his tent, Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. There he builds a second altar to the Lord and calls upon the name of the Lord. On these high stony hills the herds spread out; the man who left everything now walks the land end to end, and at every camp a stone rises up to the God who has no image, in the country full of images.
stops.quote: And there he builded an altar unto the LORD, and called upon the name of the LORD.

stops.name: The Negev, the famine and the going down
stops.campa: Abram journeys on toward the south, into the Negev. Then a famine grips the land, grievous and severe; the wells fail and the pasture browns. There is no bread. So Abram goes down into Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine is heavy in Canaan. As they near the border he looks on Sarai his wife and sees, as if for the first time, how fair a woman she is, and fear takes him for what the Egyptians will do.
stops.quote: And there was a famine in the land: and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there; for the famine was grievous in the land.

stops.name: Egypt: Sarai and Pharaoh, the plagued house
stops.campa: Say thou art my sister, Abram tells Sarai, that it may be well with me for thy sake. In Egypt the princes see her and praise her to Pharaoh, and she is taken into Pharaoh's house; Abram is dealt with well, gaining sheep, oxen, camels, servants. But the Lord strikes Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai. Pharaoh calls Abram: What is this thou hast done? Why saidst thou, She is my sister? He gives her back and sends them away, with all they have.
stops.quote: And Pharaoh called Abram, and said, What is this that thou hast done unto me? why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?

stops.name: Bethel again, return to the altar
stops.campa: Abram comes up out of Egypt, he and Sarai and Lot, very rich now in cattle, in silver, and in gold. He goes by stages from the Negev back to Bethel, to the place of the altar he made at the first, between Bethel and Ai. There again he calls on the name of the Lord. The camps of Abram and Lot are heavy with flocks, and the land can no longer bear them both together; strife breaks out between the herdsmen.
stops.quote: Unto the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first: and there Abram called on the name of the LORD.

stops.name: The parting from Lot, the plain of Jordan
stops.campa: Let there be no strife between us, Abram says to Lot, for we are brethren. Is not the whole land before thee? If thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right. Lot lifts his eyes and beholds the plain of Jordan, well watered everywhere like the garden of the Lord, and chooses it all, and journeys east, and pitches his tent toward Sodom. Abram dwells in the land of Canaan. Then the Lord tells him: Lift up thine eyes, all the land thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.
stops.quote: For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.

stops.name: Hebron, the oaks of Mamre, dwelling in the plain
stops.campa: Abram moves his tent and comes to dwell by the terebinths of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and there he builds an altar to the Lord. Under the great trees on the high Judean ridge, seven hundred metres above the sea, he settles into the land that is his by promise if not yet by deed. From here he will ride out to war to rescue Lot from the four kings, and here, returning, he will meet Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, who brings forth bread and wine and blesses him.
stops.quote: Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar unto the LORD.
